why: The statement asks whether Danzer sets (meeting every convex body of volume 1) of bounded density or bounded separation exist. No event in the record answers either part. Solomon-Weiss 2014 lowers the best known growth to T^d log T, a bound on the density question (pre-snapshot, journal-published). Simmons-Solomon (axis-parallel boxes only), Solan-Solomon-Weiss (Gowers' two-sided count condition), Tsokanos and Kashkan (dense forests, which the paper itself says need not be Danzer sets) all settle changed questions, so they are variant. Adiceam is a survey. The Kashkan thesis is unread, and what it reportedly contains is a relaxed Danzer question, so it is variant. Stefanescu and Hoshen-Samotij are neighbouring finite hitting and epsilon-net results. Erdos 224 and 1071 are different problems that share Danzer's name. Erdos 224's AI involvement was formalising a 1962 theorem, so it is none for AI and variant for scope. Kashkan's 2024 arXiv paper was reported as published in Mathematika, but the record could not confirm this, so it stays unreviewed.
doubts: The Kashkan thesis was not read, so its reported relaxed-Danzer result is unknown, and its date is known only to the year (2025). The question of whether the aligned-box sets of Simmons-Solomon transfer to convex bodies was settled only from the abstract and Wikipedia's continued listing of the problem as open.
